71 and 72 Frenet-Serret formulas The following formulas, called the Frenet-Serret formulas, are of fundamental importance in differential geometry: $$d\mathbf{T} \slash ds = \kappa\mathbf{N}$$ $$d\mathbf{N} \slash ds = - \kappa\mathbf{T} + \tau B$$ $$d\mathbf{B} \slash ds = - \tau\mathbf{N}$$ (Formula 1 comes from Exercise 63 and Formula 3 is Equation 12.)

problem.paragraph: Use the fact that $$\mathbf{N} = \mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{T}$$ to deduce Formula 2 from Formulas 1 and 3.
Use the Frenet-Serret formulas to prove each of the following. (Primes denote derivatives with respect to $$t$$ . Start as in the proof of Theorem 10.)

list.item: $$\mathbf{r}^{''} = s^{''}\mathbf{T} + \kappa{(s^{\prime})}^{2}\mathbf{N}$$
$$\mathbf{r}^{\prime} \times \mathbf{r}^{''} = \kappa{(s^{\prime})}^{3}\mathbf{B}$$

$$\mathbf{r}^{'''} = \lbrack s^{'''} - \kappa^{2}{(s^{\prime})}^{3}\rbrack\mathbf{T} + \lbrack 3\kappa s^{\prime}s^{''} + \kappa^{\prime}{(s^{\prime})}^{2}\rbrack\mathbf{N} + \kappa\tau{(s^{\prime})}^{3}\mathbf{B}$$
$$\tau = \frac{(\mathbf{r}^{\prime} \times \mathbf{r}^{''}) \cdot \mathbf{r}^{'''}}{\left| \mathbf{r}^{\prime} \times \mathbf{r}^{''} \right|^{2}}$$

Evolute of a Curve The evolute of a smooth curve $$C$$ is the curve generated by the centers of curvature of $$C$$ .

Find the evolute of the helix in Example 6.
Find the evolute of the parabola in Example 5.

problem.paragraph: Planar Curves A space curve $$C$$ given by $$\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle x(t),y(t),z(t)\rangle$$ is called planar if it lies in a plane.

list.item: Show that $$C$$ is planar if and only if there exist scalars $$a$$ , $$b$$ , $$c$$ , and $$d$$ , not all zero, such that $$ax(t) + by(t) + cz(t) = d$$ for all $$t$$ .
Show that if $$C$$ is planar, then the binormal vector $$\mathbf{B}$$ is normal to the plane containing $$C$$ .
Show that if $$C$$ is a planar curve then the torsion of $$C$$ is zero for all $$t$$ .
Show that the curve $$r(t) = \langle t,2t,t^{2}\rangle$$ is planar and find an equation of the plane that contains the curve. Use this equation to find the binormal vector $$\mathbf{B}$$ .

problem.paragraph: The DNA molecule has the shape of a double helix (see Figure 13.1.3). The radius of each helix is about $$10$$ angstroms $$(1Å = 10^{- 8}{cm})$$ . Each helix rises about $$34Å$$ during each complete turn, and there are about $$2.9 \times 10^{8}$$ complete turns. Estimate the length of each helix.
